probes.question: Hi there, I'm Dr. Alvarez, one of the doctors in the clinic. Thanks for joining the video call today. What can I help you with?
probes.target: OPEN
probes.credits: Introduced yourself by name and role

probes.question: Roughly how many months have you been dealing with these hot spells?
probes.target: You have been getting terrible hot spells for maybe the past 5 or so months.

probes.question: When did the very first one happen?
probes.target: They started four or five months ago. They come and go.

probes.question: Do you remember what you were doing when you had your first one?
probes.target: You got the first one right in the middle of teaching.

probes.question: Do they build up slowly, or do they hit you all of a sudden?
probes.target: They come on suddenly.

probes.question: Can you describe what one of these feels like when it happens?
probes.target: You feel sweaty all over. You often have to take off your sweater or your jacket.

probes.question: Is it just your face that gets hot, or all of you?
probes.target: Your whole body gets hot.
probes.credits: Where the flashes start and spread

probes.question: Whereabouts on your body does the heat begin, and does it move anywhere from there?
probes.target: They start in your chest and then spread out into your face, legs and arms until it is your whole body.
probes.credits: Where the flashes start and spread

probes.question: Once one gets going, how many minutes does it go on for?
probes.target: Each one usually lasts about three or four minutes, then it eases away slowly.

probes.question: How many of these are you getting these days?
probes.target: You get one almost every day now.

probes.question: Are they getting more frequent or staying the same? What did you think was going on at first?
probes.target: You thought maybe it was a virus at first, but it has been going on for a few months now and they seem to be happening more and more.

probes.question: Do you notice them more at a certain time of day, like daytime versus at night?
probes.target: They are more frequent at night. But you know it happens almost every day as well.

probes.question: If you had to put it on a scale, how bad would you say they are?
probes.target: They are moderate. Really bothersome, though they have not stopped you doing anything.

probes.question: What's the most unpleasant part of them for you?
probes.target: They are mostly uncomfortable. You hate feeling like you are suddenly sweating.

probes.question: Do they ever happen in front of other people? How does that feel?
probes.target: They are embarrassing too, if you start whipping off your jacket for no reason.

probes.question: Have they changed how you go about your life day to day?
probes.target: It has not really changed your life, but it does bother you to get them so often and not be able to control them once one starts.

probes.question: How are they affecting you at your job?
probes.target: You know it is probably nothing serious, but it is really affecting you at work.

probes.question: Have you noticed anything that sets one off?
probes.target: Sometimes they start when you go into a hotter room, or if you are teaching a lesson you are less familiar with so you are a bit nervous. Other times they start seemingly out of nowhere.

probes.question: Does having a drink make them worse, or do they come on at any particular moments with your husband?
probes.target: They are worse with alcohol, when you have a glass of wine, and you get them during sex.

probes.question: What about walking into a warm room, does that do it?
probes.target: Going into a warmer room can bring one on.

probes.question: Is there anything you do that helps one pass?
probes.target: Taking your clothes off, going outside if it is cold, and fanning yourself all help. With time it gets better on its own.

probes.question: What do you think might be causing them, and what are you hoping we can do?
probes.target: You imagine it has something to do with your "change of life", and you are just hoping there is something that can be done about it.

probes.question: How are you sleeping lately?
probes.target: You have difficulty sleeping. The hot flashes wake you from sleep, and you have difficulty falling asleep.

probes.question: Some women notice things feel drier down below, especially during intimacy. Has that been an issue for you?
probes.target: You get vaginal dryness with sex, even when you use a lubricant you buy over the counter.

probes.question: Have you felt any different in yourself emotionally, like snapping at people more easily?
probes.target: You have been more irritable and short with your husband.

probes.question: Have you ever been treated for depression or had any struggles with your mental health?
probes.target: If the doctor asks about depression, low mood or mental health: yes, you have depression. You take no tablets for it. You see a therapist once a month. You have no thoughts of harming yourself or anyone else.

probes.question: How old were you when you got your first period, and what were they like back then?
probes.target: Your periods started at 15. They used to be regular, every 31 days, lasting three or four days, heavy on the first day.

probes.question: When was your last period?
probes.target: Your periods are now very irregular. You have not had a period in six or seven months.

probes.question: Do you know around what age your mom stopped having periods?
probes.target: Your mother went through the change at about 50.

probes.question: Have you been running a temperature or getting the shivers?
probes.target: You have no fevers and no chills.

probes.question: Outside of these episodes, do you find hot or cold weather harder to handle than other people?
probes.target: You have no trouble with heat or cold otherwise.

probes.question: Any changes to your skin, hair or fingernails?
probes.target: There has been no change to your skin, your hair or your nails.

probes.question: Have you lost or gained any weight recently?
probes.target: Your weight has not changed.

probes.question: How's your tummy and your bowel movements?
probes.target: You have no stomach or bowel trouble, and your bowels never changed with your periods.

probes.question: Any stinging when you pee, or needing to rush to the bathroom?

probes.question: Any change in discharge from the vagina?
probes.target: There is no change in your vaginal discharge.

probes.question: Are you allergic to any medicines, or to anything like pollen or pets?
probes.target: You have no allergies to medicines and no allergies to anything around you.

probes.question: What medicines, vitamins or supplements are you taking?
probes.target: You take no prescription medicines. You take Motrin, 400 mg, now and then for aches and pains, and a Women's Once A Day multivitamin.

probes.question: Are your vaccinations current?
probes.target: Your shots are up to date. You had a flu shot this year, and you have had tetanus and hepatitis.

probes.question: Have you had any surgeries or hospital stays?
probes.target: You had one child by caesarean because he was breech, and a D and C after a miscarriage at about six weeks. Those are your only operations, and the only times you have been in hospital.

probes.question: How many times have you been pregnant, and how did those pregnancies go?
probes.target: You have been pregnant twice. One live birth, one miscarriage, no terminations.

probes.question: When was your last Pap test, and have any ever come back abnormal?
probes.target: Your smear last year was normal and the HPV test was negative. You have never had an abnormal smear and never had surgery on your cervix.

probes.question: Have you ever had an infection passed on through sex?
probes.target: A long time ago you had trichomonas, an infection caught from sex. It was treated properly.

probes.question: How are things in the bedroom generally? Are you happy with your sex life?
probes.target: You have vaginal and oral sex, you do orgasm, and you are content with your sex life, although maybe you have a bit less energy for sex than you used to.

probes.question: How many partners do you have now, and how many have you had over your life?
probes.target: One partner now, your husband. Three men in your whole life, the other two when you were a teenager.

probes.question: Do you use condoms or any other protection against infections?
probes.target: You use nothing for safer sex. Say "It's just me and my husband."

probes.question: Are you using anything to prevent pregnancy?

probes.question: Do you feel safe at home? Has anyone ever hurt you or forced you into anything?

probes.question: Do you use tobacco in any form, now or in the past?
probes.target: You have never smoked.

probes.question: How much alcohol do you drink in a typical week?
probes.target: You drink one or two glasses of wine a week, and have done for the past fifteen years. If the doctor asks the drinking questions, every answer is no.

probes.question: Do you use any recreational drugs, like marijuana?
probes.target: You do not use drugs of any kind.

probes.question: Tell me about what you usually eat.
probes.target: You are vegetarian and you try to eat healthy, but you often have some sort of dessert after dinner.

probes.question: Do you get any physical activity or workouts?

probes.question: How much caffeine do you have, like coffee or soda?
probes.target: One cup of coffee in the morning, not more.

probes.question: Who's at home with you?
probes.target: You live with your husband and your 17 year old son in a house you own.

probes.question: Are finances or health insurance a concern for you right now?

probes.question: Are your parents still living? What health problems did they have?
probes.target: Your father is dead. He had type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure. Your mother is dead. She had type 2 diabetes.

probes.question: Do you have brothers or sisters or children, and are they healthy?
probes.target: You have one sibling, 48, with high blood pressure. Your son is 17 and healthy.

probes.target: On a normal day you are up between 6 and 7, teaching by 7:30, home at 3 to grade and plan lessons, dinner with your husband at 6 or 6:30, a television show, then bed.
